newsitem.title: UK: Orange wins backing for overseas ambitions.
newsitem.headline: Orange wins backing for overseas ambitions.

text.p: UK mobile telephone company Orange Plc confirmed on Monday that its overseas expansion plans could be backed either by its parent Hutchison Whampoa or by financial institutions willing to offer attractive rates.

Assuaging some investor fears that the overseas plans of the UK's newest mobile operator may depress its short-term financial performance, a company spokesman told Reuters that a number of institutions had said that they might offer reasonable loans.
He added: "As an alternative approach, Hutchison Whampoa has indicated its willingness to undertake or participate in the investment..."

Under such a deal, Orange could take on the roll-out of the mobile network under a management contract and would then have the option to buy out Hutchison's interest over time. But Orange declined to comment on the size of any Hutchison investment.

Orange, majority-owned by Hutchison and part-owned by British Aerospance, is planning to bid formally for a mobile licence in the Netherlands in the third quarter of 1997. In an auction, brokers ABN AMRO Hoare Govett expects the licence to fetch $200 million.
Orange is also keen to get a foothold in Greece at about the same time.
The Greek national wireless operator OTE is expected next month to complete a selection process choosing an international partner to take a 30 percent stake in its cellular arm.

While anlaysts are tipping Belgium and Austria as further likely expansion targets for the company, Orange declined to comment. It noted only that most European licence opportunities will be based on the same DCS 1800 technology which it uses.
"We will be looking at the most attractive ones," the spokesman said.
Orange's shares, which have been trading 24 percent below their highs of last year, moved up 3.0p to 213p on Monday.
As the company heads towards final results in March, ABN AMRO tips a share price target of 220p -- although this is still well short of the company's 260p per share year high.

Orange raised 1.2 billion stg via a debt facility in December 1995. Since then, it has withdrawn about 700 million stg. ABN AMRO estimates that the firm will spend 330 million stg in the UK in the next two years, partly to boost its cover to 95 percent of the population.
With positive cashflow from the UK network business after that, this will leave Orange in a position to use the rest of this debt facility for non-UK business, the broker adds.

Analysts expect Orange to move into profit at the operating level in 1998 and say it could move into the black on a clean- cash EBIDTA basis in 1997. The company posted an operating loss of 97.7 million stg in the half year to June 5, 1996.
